messages.landing.examples.heading: Give anything a memory
messages.landing.example.world.title: A fictional world
messages.landing.example.world.user1: Who knows that Captain Ilya is an impostor?
messages.landing.example.world.answer1:
Two people know. **Mira the cartographer** worked it out in session 12: the tattoo on Ilya's right arm gave him away, and the real Ilya lost that arm before the war.

The **harbourmaster** has known from the start — he forged the ship's papers himself and keeps the originals locked in his desk.
messages.landing.example.world.user2: Right, the tattoo! And whose ship is the Vesper, really?
messages.landing.example.world.answer2: On paper, the crown's. The Vesper was seized as a prize during the war and never returned — which is exactly the leverage the harbourmaster holds over Ilya.
messages.landing.example.place.title: A living place
messages.landing.example.place.user1: The sulphur burner alone didn't stop the mildew in the north greenhouse — worth noting so we don't repeat it.
messages.landing.example.place.remember1: The sulphur burner alone did not stop the mildew in the north greenhouse.
messages.landing.example.place.answer2:
Three things together, in this order:
1. clearing out the citrus cuttings that blocked the airflow
2. the inline fan Nils lent us in March, run at night only
3. watering in the mornings instead of the evenings
messages.landing.example.project.title: A project
messages.landing.example.project.user1: Why did we abandon the original sync protocol?
messages.landing.example.project.answer1: Conflicts, not performance. It merged edits field by field, so two people touching the same card got a hybrid neither had written.
messages.landing.example.project.answer2: That's the one — the merge week that cost us the sprint. We switched to last-write-wins per card the week after, and nobody has asked for the old protocol back.
messages.landing.faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
messages.landing.faq.model.question: Which model is used?
messages.landing.faq.model.body: DeepSeek. An open model, so using memex supports open science. Please be aware that memex is built to remember what you tell it, not to guard your secrets, so you probably shouldn't use it as a password manager.
messages.landing.faq.free.question: How is this free?
messages.landing.faq.free.body: Memex is early-stage, and the intent is to keep it free. We're exploring donation-based ways to cover the costs, but the aim is a community-run utility, not a product.
messages.landing.faq.data.question: Where is the data stored?
messages.landing.faq.data.body: In Europe, on servers run by Resolve, the R&D unit behind memex. By using the service you're trusting Resolve and DeepSeek with your data.
messages.settings.languageLocked: Everything I remember is stored in this language, so it can't be changed after the Memex is created.
messages.settings.appLanguageHint: Changes the app's interface language only. You can talk to Memex in any language — it answers in the language you write.
messages.settings.exportHint: Saves everything in this Memex — memories and questions.
